Welcome to the Firehouse fifty-one training department in Rez grid. This walkthrough uses the real application running from the project code, with fictional personnel and exercise data. We will follow a few connected tasks: organizing the department, dispatching a call, staffing a deployment, and documenting readiness.

The personnel page brings Wallace Boden, Kelly Severide, Stella Kidd, Sylvie Brett, and their colleagues into one roster. Stations, groups, and personnel roles describe where each member belongs. Staffing and response status answer different questions: who is available, and what are they doing now? Keep those assignments accurate before depending on the roster.

The apparatus list includes Engine fifty-one, Truck eighty-one, Squad three, and Ambulance sixty-one. The unit configuration connects an apparatus to its station and defines its crew positions. A reserve engine is marked out of service so it remains visible without appearing ready. These distinctions help departments avoid confusing a listed resource with an available resource.

Now create a Medical training call. Enter a clear name, priority, incident identifier, and a short description. Use the recipient controls to select Ambulance sixty-one. After saving the dispatch, the dashboard shows the ambulance as Responding. That confirms the recorded dispatch and status transition. This isolated environment does not send real pages, texts, or push notifications.

Open the saved call to review the incident details. At the end of the exercise, open Close Call, choose the completion outcome, and enter the closeout notes. The saved record now shows Closed and retains the narrative. Departments gain a consistent handoff from intake to review, with a record of what was entered and when the call was completed.

For planned coverage, create a deployment and link the community standby call. Enter the operational dates, then add Ambulance sixty-one and Sylvie Brett to the roster. The deployment summary brings the assigned people and apparatus together. This example is operational only. Finance, reimbursement, and external ordering require their own configuration and supporting evidence.

Readiness starts with an approved checklist. Open the Engine fifty-one daily check, choose the apparatus, and answer each required item. Submit the completed check, then inspect its detail page. This demonstration shows three passing answers and a submitted score of one hundred percent. A recorded pass is evidence of the entered check; a failed item would still need an assigned repair or follow-up.

Finally, the Records workspace contains a saved training draft with an instructor, participant, apparatus, dates, and narrative. Inventory shows the imported demonstration balances, and the calendar shows upcoming exercises. These views connect daily activity with follow-up work. Use this department to practise, verify the saved result, and decide who owns the next action.
